Principal component analysis

Source: R/describe.R
pca_compute.Rd

pca_compute() runs stats::prcomp() on a set of variables (factors and logicals coded numerically). pca_scores_join() joins the component scores back to the data.

Usage

pca_compute(
  data,
  vars,
  id_col = NULL,
  scale = TRUE,
  impute = c("none", "median")
)

pca_scores_join(pca_obj, data, id_col = NULL, n_pc = 2)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

vars

Variables (names or tidyselect).

id_col

Identifier column (default: row numbers).

scale

Scale the variables to unit variance.

impute

"none" (complete cases only) or "median" (simple median imputation, for visualisation only, never for inference).

pca_obj

Output of pca_compute().

n_pc

Number of components joined.

Value

pca_compute(): list with pca (prcomp object), ve (variance explained, %), scores (tibble with .id), keep, vars, n, impute, loadings and cor_var (correlations of the variables with the components). pca_scores_join(): the rows of data kept in the PCA, with the columns PC1, PC2, ...

Examples

pc <- pca_compute(cohort_sim, c(NFL_V0, IL6_V0, CRP_V0, MOCA_V0, UPDRS_V0, AGE), id_col = ID)
round(pc$ve, 1)
#> [1] 31.5 19.5 16.4 14.0 10.0  8.6
head(pca_scores_join(pc, cohort_sim, id_col = ID)[, c("ID", "PC1", "PC2")])
#>     ID         PC1        PC2
#> 1 P001 -2.27995419  1.0463946
#> 2 P002  0.01221179  1.4245590
#> 3 P003  1.18786860  0.9402560
#> 4 P004  1.59959226  1.2156418
#> 5 P005  0.12387455 -1.6087485
#> 6 P006 -0.57484024  0.1797266
